metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0\fswiss Helvetica;}}\f0\fs20{\b\fs28 ReaFL}\par FL Studio-style tools for REAPER's arrange view (native extension).\par\par{\b Setup:} none. Install, then restart REAPER. On first start ReaFL adds the shortcuts 1 (Default tool) and T (Mute tool) and opens a ReaFL toolbar. Keys you already use are left alone.\par\par{\b Tools:}\par\bullet Default (key 1): normal REAPER mouse behaviour.\par\bullet Mute (key T): left click an item toggles its mute (drag across items to mute/unmute them), right click deletes it. Clicks with Ctrl/Alt/Win and clicks on empty space behave normally.\par\par{\b Requirements:} REAPER 7 (tested on 7.84). No other extensions needed.\par Remove the shortcuts and toolbar with {\i ReaFL: Remove ReaFL shortcuts and toolbar}.\par Upgrading from 0.1.0 (Lua) is automatic: its shortcuts, toolbar and startup hook are converted on first start.\par}

version.author: Armaan
version.changelog: Initial release: tool modes with shortcuts (1 = Default, T = Mute) and a ReaFL toolbar. Mute tool: left click toggles an item's mute (selection untouched), right click deletes it.

version.author: Armaan
version.changelog:
Rewritten as a native REAPER extension (C++). No setup script any more.
- Install via ReaPack and restart: shortcuts 1 (Default tool) and T (Mute tool) and a ReaFL toolbar are added automatically on first start. Keys you already bound are left alone, and if you remove them they stay removed. - Mute tool now intercepts arrange-view clicks natively (no js_ReaScriptAPI needed, no mouse modifier changes): - left click toggles an item's mute without changing the selection - drag across items to mute/unmute them all (the first item decides), one undo point - right click deletes the item (undoable), no context menu - double-clicks do nothing extra; clicks with Ctrl/Alt/Win and clicks on empty space behave normally - New actions: "ReaFL: Remove ReaFL shortcuts and toolbar" and "ReaFL: Reinstall default shortcuts and toolbar". - Upgrading from 0.1.0 converts its shortcuts and toolbar to the new actions, removes the `__startup.lua` hook and clears its saved state.

version.author: Armaan
version.changelog: - In the Mute tool (and any future non-Default tool) REAPER's own left/right click and drag behaviour is now blocked everywhere in the arrange area, including empty space and below the last track: no marquee selection, deselecting, edit cursor moves, item moves or context menu. Clicks on items still mute / delete as before. - Right click on empty arrange space no longer opens the context menu in the Mute tool. - Ctrl / Alt / Win (Cmd / Option / Control) clicks in the arrange area are blocked too while a tool is active, so a tool never falls back to REAPER's mouse actions. They don't mute or delete either; use the Default tool (1) for REAPER's modifier clicks. - Still passed through: mouse wheel (scroll / zoom with any modifiers), middle button, hover, the keyboard (including the menu key context menu), and everything outside the arrange area (ruler, track panel, scrollbars, mixer, other windows). - A press that started in the Default tool finishes normally if you switch tools mid-drag, and a blocked press always releases the mouse capture on button-up (or when capture is lost), so drags can't get stuck.

version.author: Armaan
version.changelog: - FL's delete animation: every item a ReaFL tool deletes (Delete click/drag, Draw/Paint/Mute right button, Slice right-button cut-and-delete) leaves a pale grey rounded "ghost" in its place that only fades (clear for ~115 ms, gone by ~480 ms; several overlap, each on its own clock). The item itself is deleted at once; the ghost touches no project state and makes no undo point, follows scroll/zoom, and is not shown for undo or REAPER's own delete. Off switch: `[ReaFL] delete_ghost=0` in `reaper-extstate.ini` (or `SetExtState("ReaFL","delete_ghost","0",true)`). Test API: `ReaFL_Test_Ghosts`, `ReaFL_Test_GhostClock`. - Always-on log file `<resource path>/ReaFL/reafl.log` (1 MB cap, one `.old` kept) with version/platform, tool switches, setup/migration actions and console messages. - Code split into building blocks (click blocking, gesture engine, item actions, one undo point per gesture, cursors); tools are declared in `src/tools/catalog.cpp`. - Tools show their own cursor everywhere in the arrange view (REAPER's hover cursor changes are overridden); Mute uses REAPER's arrow-with-✕ cursor (`arrowdel`, shared with Delete). - Right-click delete now makes its undo point when the button is released. - New tools with toggle actions, default keys and toolbar buttons: Draw (P), Paint (B), Delete (D), Slip (S), Slice (C), Select (E), Zoom (Z), Playback (Y). Each blocks REAPER's mouse in the arrange area and has its own cursor. Draw and Paint: right click deletes an item, right drag deletes every item passed over (one undo point). The rest do nothing yet. - Draw (P), left button: a click in empty space places a copy of the brush item at the nearest grid line on the track under the mouse; keep the button held and the copy follows the mouse (across tracks). On an item: click selects it and makes it the brush, drag the body to move it (snapped, to the track under the mouse), drag an edge to resize it from that side, double-click a MIDI item to open the MIDI editor. Edge/body cursors. - Paint (B), left button: a click places one copy; a drag paints back-to-back copies along the start track, skipping over existing items (vertical drags add nothing). Items: as Draw. - Delete (D), left or right button: a click (or double-click) deletes the item under the mouse, a drag deletes every item it touches, horizontally or vertically; one undo point per click or drag. Shift and Alt act as plain (also Alt pressed mid-drag). Ctrl+click selects only that item, Ctrl+drag draws a box and selects every item it touches, replacing the selection (nothing deleted, no undo point). - The brush is the item last clicked, moved or resized with Draw or Paint (audio or MIDI). Copies are pooled: MIDI copies share the brush's MIDI pool, audio copies the same file and take settings. It is saved with the project and in ReaFL's state, so it survives tool switches and reopening; if the brush item was deleted its saved copy is still used. Every Draw/Paint action is one undo point ("ReaFL: Draw item", "Paint 3 items", "Move item", "Resize item"). - Updating from 0.2.x adds the new keys (unless you use them) and toolbar buttons once; keys/buttons you removed are not re-added. - Mute: a left drag may start on empty space (the first item reached decides mute or unmute); a right drag deletes every item passed over (one undo point). - Remove then Reinstall: removing the shortcuts now also drops the "disabled default" key lines REAPER saves for the keys ReaFL had taken, so REAPER's own default actions for P, D, S, C, E, Z, Y come back after the restart. - Draw/Paint: picking the brush deselects other items without a separate "Unselect all items" undo point, so every Draw/Paint action undoes in one step. - Item hit-testing falls back to arrange geometry when another window covers the arrange view at that point. - Slice (C): left click on an item cuts it at the nearest grid line (exact pointer time with snap off); a left drag shows a vertical preview line at the snapped position over the tracks from the press row to the current row, and on release cuts every item on those tracks there (vertical, horizontal or diagonal drags). Right click/drag (may start on empty space) cuts and deletes the piece nearest the mouse. Ctrl+click selects the item, Ctrl+drag box-selects; Shift+drag cuts only the item under the release point; Shift/Alt clicks and double-clicks' second click do nothing. Both pieces keep mute and content (audio take offset continues); slicing clears the selection; one undo point per gesture ("ReaFL: Slice item" / "Slice 3 items"). Wheel, zoom and middle drag still reach REAPER. - Hidden tracks and the children of a collapsed folder are untouchable by every tool (clicks, drags and Slice lines skip them; a drag below the last track stops at the last visible one). Locked items are ignored by every hit-test. A drag that leaves the arrange view hits nothing outside it (items scrolled out of view are never edited blind); a Slice drag released outside the view cuts at the view's edge, where its line is drawn. - Draw/Paint: a move or resize that ends where it started (e.g. at the minimum length) restores the item exactly and makes no undo point. - Alt disables snapping while held, in every tool that snaps (Draw new/move/resize, Paint, Slice cut and preview line), also mid-drag. Releasing Alt mid-drag works as in FL: Slice snaps to the grid again; Draw (new, move, resize) keeps the off-grid offset the item had at Alt-up and moves in whole grid steps from there; Paint snaps only at the press (unless Alt is held at the press), so Alt later changes nothing. An Alt press in Draw/Paint acts like a plain press (previously blocked). - FL parity (FL re-runs of Oct 30): Draw Shift+drag in empty space fill-paints like Paint (one undo point); Shift+drag on an item makes a pooled clone on the item's own track ("ReaFL: Clone item", the brush stays the original); Ctrl on an item selects it without moving it, Ctrl+drag in empty space box-selects. A double-click on an item in Draw/Paint runs REAPER's own item double-click mouse modifier (MIDI editor / item properties by default, or whatever is configured) and adds no undo point. Paint Shift places one copy at the release point (snapped, press track); Paint Ctrl does nothing. Draw/Paint item body cursor: REAPER's arrow with 4-way cross (`cur00001`). Mute: Alt acts as plain, a plain press clears the item selection, Ctrl+click selects that item and Ctrl+drag box-selects (nothing muted). Selection changes never make undo points (FL records them). - ReaScript API for in-process tests (`ReaFL_GetTool`, `ReaFL_SetTool`, `ReaFL_Log`, `ReaFL_GetBrush`, `ReaFL_Test_*`, including `ReaFL_Test_AutoAnswer` for message boxes, `ReaFL_Test_Overlay` and `ReaFL_Test_DoubleClickAction`) and Lua tests in `tests/`, plus box helpers (restart, Remove/Reinstall cycle, real-pointer cursor check).
